body: With the growing prevalence of large language model (LLM) generated content, watermarking is considered a promising approach for attributing text to LLMs and distinguishing it from human-written content. A prominent class of techniques embeds subtle but detectable signals in generated text by modifying token sampling probabilities. However, such methods are unsuitable for open-source models, where users have white-box access and can easily disable watermarking during inference. In this work, we introduce OpenStamp, a watermarking technique that encodes the watermarking logic directly into the model weights by modifying only the final projection, or unembedding, layer. Through experiments across two models, we show that OpenStamp achieves superior detection performance, with minimal degradation in model capabilities compared to prior methods. The implanted watermark is explicitly designed, and empirically confirmed, to be more robust to paraphrasing attacks and harder to scrub off through post-hoc fine-tuning than prior open-source watermarks. To enable developers to watermark their models, we release our code alongside watermarked versions of 4 popular open-source models.
summaryZh: 针对传统采样修改类水印在开源模型中容易被白盒用户禁用或通过微调擦除的问题，本文推出了OpenStamp水印技术。该技术仅通过修改最终的投影（unembedding）层，将水印逻辑直接编码进模型权重中。实验表明，OpenStamp在对改写攻击和微调表现出极高鲁棒性的同时，对模型原本能力的损害降至最低，并且作者开源了相关代码及4个热门开源模型的加水印版本。
